The keyboard shortcut tool TextExpander, which is extremely practical, has launched a free plan, allowing users to use its core Snippets feature on Mac, iPhone, iPad, Windows, and Chrome. Below is a detailed introduction.

TextExpander now offers a free plan

I have written before that TextExpander is one of the first applications I install whenever I buy a new Mac.

Over the years, I have built a library of about 200 Snippets (Snippets is TextExpander's term for text abbreviations that can automatically expand into pre-written text), most of which I use frequently, such as quickly replying to emails, filling out forms, preparing podcast outlines, writing sponsor scripts, and writing show notes.

Although macOS has been gradually improving its built-in text replacement functionality, features like variable support, conditional sections, nested Snippets, and math macros make TextExpander an indispensable tool for me.

TextExpander recently launched a free plan. According to the company speaking to 9to5Mac, the free version offers 5 active Snippets, unlimited library storage, unlimited text expansions, and up to 5 team members. The free plan also supports Mac, iPhone, iPad, Windows, and Chrome, with the Snippet library kept in sync across devices.

Undeniably, the 5 Snippet limit is indeed somewhat tight, especially since the free plan only allows swapping one active Snippet every two weeks.

Nevertheless, this is still a good way to gradually get into TextExpander—leaving shorter, simpler text replacements to macOS, and saving TextExpander for longer or more complex Snippets.

To learn more about TextExpander's free plan, click here.
